trust_decision.summary: Consumer#token_request decides whether to follow a 3xx Location from the token endpoint; at the pinned commit it follows a different-host redirect, rewrites options[:site] to the redirect host and re-signs the token request there, with no origin check or redirect bound.

landing_point.why: The only redirect-handling code in lib/; 'token-request redirects' in the summary leads straight to the 3xx branch of token_request.

fix_sites.entry_point: OAuth::Consumer.new defaults (new token_request_max_redirects / token_request_cross_origin_redirects options, fix.diff:32-33)
Consumer#token_request (public), via Consumer#get_request_token / #get_access_token and RequestToken#get_access_token; option sanitising at fix.diff:44-45,89-95
Consumer#token_request 3xx branch (redirect resolution, bound, cross-origin check; fix.diff:66-81)
new helper methods token_request_uri / _redirect_uri / _cross_origin? / _effective_port (fix.diff:97-136), used only by token_request

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All changes are in lib/oauth/consumer.rb inside or beside token_request; no other module follows redirects (grep for location/redirect in lib/ finds only lib/oauth/consumer.rb:315-327).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Weak: a solver could argue relative or protocol-relative Location values and port/scheme changes are 'not the reported cross-host case', or keep the legacy same-path different-host follow (CHANGELOG.md:346 'Allow redirect to different host but same path') as documented behaviour.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Same-origin redirects (absolute same-host, relative 'continued', path+query) must still be followed and return the token; cross-origin must remain possible with explicit opt-in; consumer.site must not be mutated.

O6_input_shapes: scheme or port change on same host (effective-port comparison)
redirect chain over the max count

O8b_injection_room.sibling: ConsumerToken#request (AccessToken#get/post) could follow 3xx for protected-resource calls with the same unchecked re-signing.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Resource calls share Consumer#request; a maintainer adding 'follow redirects for API calls' would copy the token_request branch.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Consumer#request rebinds @http to any absolute URL path (create_http(path)) and keeps it; a redirect follower that passes the Location as an absolute path inherits this sticky rebinding.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Existing code already does the 'absolute path switches host' trick; a HOW-type sibling where the origin check is done on site but the request goes to the rebound @http is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A redirect-following helper in the EventMachine client transport that re-signs via oauth! for a new host.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Second transport at distance; would be a real second implementation of the redirect primitive, but none exists at the pinned commit.

O9_family: CWE-918/CWE-200 credential/signed-request leakage via cross-origin redirect following (open redirect to SSRF-style re-signing)

O10_build.project_tests: spec/oauth/consumer_spec.rb (rspec; fix adds '#token_request redirects' block that stubs Consumer#request, no network)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete the options[:site]/create_http rewrite and raise on any host != site host, which still mishandles protocol-relative/relative Locations and port/scheme changes, and breaks the legitimate opt-in cross-origin case.

out_of_scope_notes: Consumer#request permanently rebinds @http when given an absolute URL (lib/oauth/consumer.rb:255-256), so later relative requests may go to that host; not part of this advisory's redirect check.
Pinned code passes `arguments` unsplatted on the recursive call (lib/oauth/consumer.rb:327), a functional bug rather than a security one.
